postings.title: Production Operator
postings.description:
ABOUT CIRCUITHUB

CircuitHub is reshaping electronics manufacturing with The Grid, a factory-scale robotics platform that makes small-batch, high-mix electronics assembly radically more efficient. Think semiconductor-fab precision applied to the chaotic world of prototyping and low-volume production: a 10x throughput improvement in one of the world's most foundational industries.

We've raised $45M from top-tier investors including Plural, Y Combinator and Google Ventures, and we're already profitable. Our customers include a major EV maker, a top AI lab and many of the worlds largest companies.

The Grid isn't a prototype. It's live, scaling fast and delivering real revenue, and we're building the team that will scale it further.


THE ROLE

Join our production team as a Production Operator and help us revolutionize electronics manufacturing. You'll work hands-on with advanced automated equipment, ensuring high-quality circuit board assembly while maintaining our industry-leading speed and precision standards.

No direct experience with electronics manufacturing is necessary, but we like curious people willing to learn. You enjoy working with your hands, take pride in quality work, and thrive in a fast-paced environment where technology meets manufacturing excellence.

 


WHAT YOU'LL WORK ON

The types of work you'll do:

 - Equipment Operation - Running and monitoring automated SMT (Surface Mount Technology) lines and assembly equipment

 - Quality Control - Performing visual inspections, testing, and quality checks on assembled circuit boards

 - Material Handling - Managing component inventory, kitting parts, and maintaining organized workstation areas

 - Process Optimization - Following standard operating procedures and suggesting improvements to increase efficiency

 - Machine Maintenance - Performing routine maintenance, troubleshooting basic issues, and coordinating with technical teams

 - Documentation - Recording production data, tracking metrics, and maintaining accurate work logs

 - Safety Compliance - Following all safety protocols and maintaining a clean, organized work environment
   
    


WHAT WE'RE LOOKING FOR

You might be a great fit if:

 - You have strong attention to detail and take pride in producing quality work

 - You're comfortable working with technology and learning new automated systems

 - You can follow detailed procedures while also thinking critically about process improvements

 - You work well both independently and as part of a team

 - You're physically capable of standing for extended periods and handling small components

 - You have a positive attitude and adapt well to changing priorities in a growing company

 

Nice to have: Experience in manufacturing, electronics assembly, or working with automated equipment. Technical training or certifications in manufacturing or electronics are a plus but not required.

 


WHY CIRCUITHUB?

 - Cutting-edge technology - Work with state-of-the-art automated manufacturing equipment

 - Mission-driven work - Help shape the future of electronics manufacturing

 - Skills development - Learn advanced manufacturing techniques and automation systems

 - Growth opportunity - Fast-growing company with opportunities for advancement

 - Collaborative environment - Work alongside engineers and technical specialists

 - Competitive benefits - Health insurance, retirement plan, and paid time off

 


WORK ENVIRONMENT

 - Clean, modern facility - Climate-controlled environment with latest safety standards

 - Multi shift schedule - Positions available on day, swing, and night shift as well as weekends

 - Team-oriented culture - Collaborative atmosphere where everyone's input matters

 - Continuous improvement - Always looking for ways to optimize processes and quality

 


INTERESTED?

Ready to be part of the future of electronics manufacturing? We'd love to hear from you—even if your experience doesn't match every point. We care about potential, work ethic, and people who are excited to grow with us.

postings.title: Software Engineer, Haskell
postings.description:
ABOUT CIRCUITHUB

CircuitHub is reshaping electronics manufacturing with The Grid, a factory-scale robotics platform that makes small-batch, high-mix electronics assembly radically more efficient. Think semiconductor-fab precision applied to the chaotic world of prototyping and low-volume production: a 10x throughput improvement in one of the world's most foundational industries.

We've raised $45M from top-tier investors including Plural, Y Combinator and Google Ventures, and we're already profitable. Our customers include a major EV maker, a top AI lab and many of the worlds largest companies.

The Grid isn't a prototype. It's live, scaling fast and delivering real revenue, and we're building the team that will scale it further.


OVERVIEW

 - CircuitHub is primarily built using a combination of Haskell, Nix, and PostgreSQL, deployed to both AWS and bare metal machines. We use a significant amount of open-source technology, and also try and give back where possible (for example, both Rel8 https://github.com/circuithub/rel8 and Fast Downward Haskell bindings https://github.com/circuithub/fast-downward).

 - CircuitHub spans a vast problem space. Challenges include computer vision (OpenCV), machine learning (PyTorch), hard optimization problems (Z3/MiniZinc/OR-Tools), and all the normal engineering challenges of building both web-based customer-facing and internal tooling.

 - We work on manufacturing execution systems, enterprise resource planning, and robotics. An old video from Haskell Exchange 2019 https://youtu.be/gl2Ze1WmrYY?si=zlFrqALU7DaPfS65&t=282 hints at what we are up to on the robotics side. We have progressed significantly since then!

 - These roles are remote (any location), in-person, or hybrid, depending on preference.

 - We have offices in South Deerfield - USA, Cambridge, and London, UK.

 - Salary depends on the candidate and location, but as guidance in the UK, a likely range is £80k to £125k and in the US $125k to $250k, with additional equity.

 - CircuitHub has raised $45M from top-tier VCs and has been going for about ten years. CircuitHub is profitable, with tens of millions in revenue. Small team (CircuitHub is ~50 employees) with tremendous growth opportunity and low risk. We are aiming to 10x capacity through 2027 in both our existing Massachusetts factory and expand into Europe.

 


TEAM/ENVIRONMENT/ROLE

Our R&D team is more than 20 people, with eight engineers working directly on the Haskell code base. We are looking to expand the team significantly this year. We have many exciting problems to solve, from robotic path planning to more conventional web products.

We are happy to consider candidates without commercial Haskell experience, but your other skills and experience would need to compensate. A possible profile, for instance, would be a professional robotics background with some hobbyist FP experience.

Conversely, for experienced Haskellers without experience in our domain, we will look for interests that correlate with what we are trying to accomplish. Life is too short to work on something you are not passionate about!

 


LOCATION

Work remotely, or from one of our offices in the UK (London, Cambridge) or USA (Boston)

postings.title: Mechanical Build Engineer
postings.description:
ABOUT CIRCUITHUB

CircuitHub is reshaping electronics manufacturing with The Grid, a factory-scale robotics platform that makes small-batch, high-mix electronics assembly radically more efficient. Think semiconductor-fab precision applied to the chaotic world of prototyping and low-volume production: a 10x throughput improvement in one of the world's most foundational industries.

We've raised $45M from top-tier investors including Plural, Y Combinator and Google Ventures, and we're already profitable. Our customers include a major EV maker, a top AI lab and many of the worlds largest companies.

The Grid isn't a prototype. It's live, scaling fast and delivering real revenue, and we're building the team that will scale it further.

What We’re Looking For

We are assembling a team of system build engineers to scale the production of our factory automation systems. We are looking for people who are excited to build robotics, whether that be high speed gantries, novel end effectors, custom assembly tooling, laser enclosures, chemical handling systems and everything in between. If you love to build things, this role could be for you!

 

Critically, you should be comfortable interpreting 3D CAD assemblies and building from them directly. We use Fusion 360, but a basic familiarity with Fusion 360 or other leading CAD systems (Solidworks, Inventor, Creo, Catia, NX, Onshape) in a professional or hobbyist setting is a must.

 

Experience with PLC commissioning/debugging, particularly Beckhoff TwinCAT, CNC machining and cabinet wiring would be bonuses here.

 

This role would be excellent for (but not limited to!) recent graduates, newly qualified apprentices, maintenance technicians, machinists, makers and more. If you want to build things and can spin CAD we want to hear from you.

 

We are flexible on how you want to work; this is a hands-on, onsite role but the hours and schedule aren’t rigid. We would be delighted to accommodate part time or adjusted schedules to suit caring/childcare or other obligations outside of work. Would you prefer a non-traditional work schedule? Talk to us!

 

What you’ll do

 - Build up full automation systems from a mixture of custom and off-the-shelf parts, anything from hand-held end effectors to multi-tonne high speed gantries

 - Take a role in commissioning and testing

 - Liaise with logistics partners for system shipment

 - Work through any design issues by feeding back to the design team and making your own design changes

 - General workshop tasks such as tidying, consumable stocking and machinery cleaning

 

What CircuitHub Can Offer

Salary, £35,000 - £60,000 dependent on experience

 

A candidate at the lower end of this range might be expected to:

 - Be able to build mechatronic assemblies from 3D CAD

 - Carry out basic troubleshooting tasks such as selecting the correct fasteners, torquing to the correct values, pressing bearings and feeding back design issues to the wider team.

 - Work safely in a dynamic, constantly evolving workshop environment

 

A candidate at the higher end of this range might additionally be able to do some of the following:

 - carry out small component design changes as part of assembly troubleshooting

 - Carry out some TwinCAT drive commissioning

 - Be confident in basic troubleshooting of a wiring cabinet

 - Set up/program a CNC mill

 

Think you can do more than this? Great! The salary range is not a hard limit, if you are an expert on all of the above we still want to talk to you.

 

Not quite so experienced, but passionate and want to learn? Also great! Talk to us, we might be able to find a place for you.

 

Location

This is an onsite role out of our site in central Cambridge working alongside a driven team of automation engineers who are designing, building and supporting the expansion of our Grid PCB assembly system.

postings.title: Software Engineer, Robotics
postings.description:
ABOUT CIRCUITHUB

CircuitHub is reshaping electronics manufacturing with The Grid, a factory-scale robotics platform that makes small-batch, high-mix electronics assembly radically more efficient. Think semiconductor-fab precision applied to the chaotic world of prototyping and low-volume production: a 10x throughput improvement in one of the world's most foundational industries.

We've raised $45M from top-tier investors including Plural, Y Combinator and Google Ventures, and we're already profitable. Our customers include a major EV maker, a top AI lab and many of the worlds largest companies.

The Grid isn't a prototype. It's live, scaling fast and delivering real revenue, and we're building the team that will scale it further.


WHAT YOU'LL DO

 - Architect the robot operating system. Design the core abstractions: how robots, cameras, tools and jobs are modelled, how work is planned and dispatched, how state is shared and how failures are handled. Decide what belongs in Python and what needs Rust.

 - Bring in new vision. Integrate novel computer vision algorithms into the control loop, from finding and centring parts to checking every pick and placement, and make them fast and reliable enough for production.

 - Build agentic robotics. Put large models to work in the robots themselves: programming a new part from its datasheet, judging a pick from a camera image, diagnosing a fault and recovering from it, with evals that prove it works before it runs alone.

 - Move a fleet. Route dozens of movers at once without collisions or deadlocks, and coordinate gantries, printers and ovens around them.

 - Bridge to real time. Design clean interfaces between high-level planning and the real-time controllers driving the motors.

 - Make it observable. Simulation, tracing and replay, so every change is proven before it reaches the factory and every failure can be explained.


WHAT WE LOOK FOR

 - You've worked on, and ideally architected, a large-scale robot code base that ran on real hardware in production.

 - Strong software engineering in Python and Rust (or C++ and a willingness to move to Rust). You care about types, testing, concurrency and clear architecture.

 - Experience with some of: motion or path planning, multi-robot coordination, controls, perception, scheduling.

 - Hands-on experience applying large models (LLMs or vision-language models) to robotics, or a strong drive to.

 - You use coding agents to move faster and take full ownership of what they produce.

 - You're happy to visit our factories in the US and UK to see your code run.


STACK

 - Robot software: Python and Rust

 - Vision and models: OpenCV, PyTorch, ONNX Runtime, Claude and OpenAI APIs

 - Planning: multi-agent path-finding, OR-Tools

 - Data and observability: PostgreSQL, OpenTelemetry, ClickHouse

 - Agents: Claude Code and Codex throughout


PAY

UK £80k–£125k · US $125k–$250k, depending on experience, plus equity.

postings.title: Software Engineer, Computer Vision
postings.description:

WHAT YOU'LL DO

 - Pick reliably. Train and deploy the models that find parts in bins and trays, centre them on the nozzle and catch a clumped or dropped pick.

 - Align precisely. Fiducial detection, calibration and image alignment for placements measured in fractions of a millimetre.

 - Build the data loop. Decide what to capture, build labelling tools, and turn operator verdicts into training data.

 - Go fast. Work with our high-speed cameras and GPU capture pipeline to move vision closer to real time.

 - Measure it. Track accuracy in production, find where errors come from, and prove every change against past results.


WHAT WE LOOK FOR

 - You've shipped computer vision into production, beyond a notebook.

 - Strong software engineering in Python, C++ or a comparable language.

 - A mix of classical vision (geometry, calibration, template matching) and deep learning; you know when each is the right tool.

 - Experience with industrial or machine-vision cameras is a bonus.

 - You use coding agents to move faster and take full ownership of what they produce.

 - You like the physical world: lighting, lenses and parts rotated by 90°.


STACK

 - Vision: OpenCV, PyTorch and Lightning, ONNX Runtime on GPU, libtorch from Haskell

 - Cameras: Basler GigE cameras via pylon, high-speed cameras with GPUDirect capture

 - Services: Python and Haskell, PostgreSQL, Nix and NixOS


PAY

UK £80k–£125k · US $125k–$250k, depending on experience, plus equity.

postings.title: Software Engineer, Product
postings.description:

Think semiconductor-fab precision applied to the chaotic world of prototyping and low-volume production: a 10x throughput improvement in one of the world's most foundational industries.

We've raised $45M from top-tier investors including Plural, Y Combinator and Google Ventures, and we're already profitable. Our customers include a major EV maker, a top AI lab and many of the worlds largest companies.

The Grid isn't a prototype. It's live, scaling fast and delivering real revenue, and we're building the team that will scale it further.


WHAT YOU’LL DO

As a Product Engineer at CircuitHub, you will own entire production software systems end-to-end, from understanding operational problems on the factory floor through designing, building, deploying, and operating the software that solves them. You’ll be responsible for entire systems rather than isolated tickets, owning problems from discovery through deployment and operational impact.

This includes building and maintaining the internal operational stack that seamlessly connects planning, materials, purchasing, personnel, and factory processes, transforming complex manufacturing workflows into highly reliable, usable software. You’ll partner closely with factory operators, engineers, and company leadership to ensure CircuitHub’s factories scale smoothly as demand and Grid capabilities grow.

Example Projects:

 - Develop production planning tools and inventory/materials-flow systems

 - Improve factory operator workflows

 - Integrate new automation equipment

 - Apply AI and LLMs to automate operational decision making, from purchasing and production planning to machine diagnostics and debugging.

 - Build the software systems that coordinate thousands of manufacturing decisions across people, robots, inventory, and suppliers in real time.

 


WHAT WE’RE LOOKING FOR

Must-haves

 - Strong PostgreSQL experience: complex queries, performance tuning, and schema design

 - Solid data modeling and systems-design judgment

 - Hands-on systems integration: stitching together APIs, tools, and workflows that hold up in production

 - Strong software engineering fundamentals and the ability to ship production systems quickly and reliably.

 - Willingness and ability to travel regularly to CircuitHub factories (US and UK) and spend time on the factory floor partnering closely with operators and engineers.

Nice-to-haves

 - Familiarity with manufacturing, logistics, ERP/MRP, or supply-chain systems

 - Experience building internal tools or operational software

 - Experience keeping mission-critical operational systems fast and reliable

 - Comfortable collaborating closely with internal teams on regular basis

 


WHO YOU'LL WORK WITH

You’ll work directly with the Head of Internal Software and company leadership to identify bottlenecks and turn them into software systems that improve factory throughput. You'll join the internal software team and work alongside engineers, factory operators, and leadership.

In your first 6–12 months, success looks like owning a meaningful slice of the production operations stack outright and measurably improving the reliability and throughput of the operations it supports.

 


LOCATION & WORK ENVIRONMENT

 - Offices: South Deerfield MA, US; London and Cambridge, UK

 - Flexible arrangements: remote, hybrid, or in-person

 - This is potentially a remote role open to candidates who can maintain at least four hours of daily overlap with both our US East Coast and UK teams.

 - While the role can be remote, successful candidates should expect regular travel to CircuitHub factories (in US and UK) and hands-on engagement with production operations.

 


COMPENSATION

 - UK: £80k–£125k

 - US: $125k–$250k

 - Plus equity

This is a single posting open across multiple levels. Your level and offer are calibrated to your experience, and we're happy to discuss where you'd land early in the process.

postings.title: Software Engineer, Applied AI
postings.description:
ABOUT CIRCUITHUB

CircuitHub is reshaping electronics manufacturing with The Grid, a factory-scale robotics platform that makes small-batch, high-mix electronics assembly radically more efficient. Think semiconductor-fab precision applied to the chaotic world of prototyping and low-volume production: a 10x throughput improvement in one of the world's most foundational industries.

We've raised $45M from top-tier investors including Plural, Y Combinator and Google Ventures, and we're already profitable. Our customers include a major EV maker, a top AI lab and many of the worlds largest companies.

The Grid isn't a prototype. It's live, scaling fast and delivering real revenue, and we're building the team that will scale it further.


THE ROLE

CircuitHub makes electronics on demand. Engineers upload a circuit board design; we buy the parts, build the board in our own robotic factory and ship it. More and more of that business is now run by AI agents, and we want you to help build them.

These aren't chatbots. Our agents have real jobs:

 - They inspect boards. An agent checks camera images of every panel we build for wrong, rotated or missing parts.

 - They program robots. Agents read datasheets so our pick-and-place machines know how to handle each new part.

 - They watch the factory. They spot stray parts in robot storage, diagnose printer faults and clear stuck machines.

 - They run the back office. They book supplier invoices, chase late orders, explain quotes and triage bugs.

 - They write our code. Most of what our team ships starts in an agent session.


WHAT YOU'LL DO

Find a process people still do by hand and automate it end to end: decide what needs judgement and what needs plain code, build the tools, and prove it works before it runs alone. Then make it cheaper, faster and right more often. You'll also improve the platform every agent runs on, and work closely with the people your work serves, from factory operators to finance.


HOW WE BUILD

 - Evals first. An agent earns the right to work alone: blind tests against people's verdicts, shadow runs beside the humans, replays of past decisions. We track accuracy and cost per run, and re-test whenever we change a model, a prompt or the effort level.

 - Agents judge, code writes. Agents return structured answers. Plain code checks them against a second source and makes every change.

 - Classical first, model second. Cheap vision and maths narrow the problem so the model only looks where it matters.

 - Safe by construction. Agents work in sandboxed cloud machines that never hold real credentials, and tool calls are built so a business action can't run twice.


RECENT WORK

 - Image alignment ranks the parts on each board photo. The worst 20% of parts hold about 90% of real defects, so the agent only inspects those. In a blind re-run it caught all 13 defects operators had marked.

 - A photo check for stray parts in robot storage scored 10 out of 10 blind, at about 8¢ a photo. The model it replaced caught about half.

 - Agent tool calls leave durable receipts, so a session killed mid-deploy resumes without sending the same email or order twice.

 - Invoices extracted from supplier emails matched what a person had entered 66 times out of 66.

 - A constraint solver replans the whole factory every two minutes, across robots, ovens and people.


WHAT WE LOOK FOR

 - You've put LLM agents into production and can tell us what broke and how you knew it was working.

 - You're a strong software engineer first. Most of this job is real engineering, not prompting: concurrency, idempotency, data modelling, security.

 - You build the eval before you trust the result.

 - You like the physical world: cameras, robots, parts rotated by 90°.

 - Bonus: computer vision, optimisation or electronics.


STACK

 - Agents: Claude Code, Codex, Claude and OpenAI APIs, MCP, skills in plain Markdown

 - Code: TypeScript (Bun, React), Python (FastAPI, Dagster, OpenCV, OR-Tools), PostgreSQL

 - Infra: Nix and NixOS, Nomad, Terraform, Vault, AWS, Modal sandboxes, OpenTelemetry


PAY

UK £80k–£125k · US $125k–$250k, depending on experience, plus equity.

postings.title: Mechatronics Engineer
postings.description:
ABOUT CIRCUITHUB

CircuitHub is reshaping electronics manufacturing with The Grid, a factory-scale robotics platform that makes small-batch, high-mix electronics assembly radically more efficient. Think semiconductor-fab precision applied to the chaotic world of prototyping and low-volume production: a 10x throughput improvement in one of the world's most foundational industries.

We've raised $45M from top-tier investors including Plural, Y Combinator and Google Ventures, and we're already profitable. Our customers include a major EV maker, a top AI lab and many of the worlds largest companies.

The Grid isn't a prototype. It's live, scaling fast and delivering real revenue, and we're building the team that will scale it further.


THE ROLE

Mechatronics Engineers at CircuitHub own projects end to end. You'll start with a problem, often on our factory floor, and take it all the way to a working machine:

 - Understand the problem and turn it into a clear specification

 - Generate ideas and choose the right mechanism

 - Design it in CAD and prove it out with the engineering calculations

 - Prototype and build it, machining parts in our in-house CNC shop

 - Bring it to life with software on our in-house robotics operating system

We work AI-first. AI tools help you scope the problem, drive your CAD, run the calculations and write the machine software. The software side needs basic software engineering skills, not a software background: you'll write it with AI agents, supported by a dedicated software engineering team who build the operating system.

You must have built things before, ideally robots, whether as a hobbyist, student, employee or founder. We don't hire narrow specialists. We want engineers who can:

 - Diagnose system-wide failures from first principles

 - Prototype mechanical and software fixes on the fly

 - Work autonomously and communicate clearly with a team spread across sites

 - Take responsibility for how their machines perform in live production


THINGS YOU'LL DO

This is a design role with hands-on prototyping. For example:

 - Conceive new mechanisms to handle electronics parts and other robotic handling tasks, using AI to scope and specify the problem

 - Design gantries and end effectors in Fusion 360

 - Use AI agents to run the engineering calculations, and know when to distrust them

 - Machine prototype parts in our in-house CNC shop

 - Analyse end-effector behaviour from video and revise its geometry and control approach to improve throughput and reliability

 - Program machine behaviour on our in-house robotics operating system, with AI agents doing the heavy lifting

 - Specify sensors that catch errors while a machine is running, or monitor a chemical process

 - Prototype and deploy a new test robot for in-line PCB validation

 - Commission your machines and hand them over to our build team to scale up

 - Work across our US and UK sites to share what you've learned and shape the roadmap


BONUS SKILLS

 - Experience programming machines, whether PLCs, robot controllers, embedded systems or Python

 - Programming and running CNC machinery

 - Design of chemical handling machinery

 - Optics


PAY AND LEVEL

£45K–£125K depending on experience, plus equity.

A candidate at the lower end of the range might have:

 - Built some systems before, with some exposure to robotics or automation

 - Seen parts and subsystems through to manufacture as part of a design team

 - Knowledge of designing for machining

 - A keen interest in moving their career towards practical robotics

A candidate at the upper end might also have:

 - Led the build and deployment of large-scale automated systems

 - Written the software that controls their own machines

 - Designed for a wide range of manufacturing methods, from machining to sheet metal to injection moulding

 - Mentored more junior engineers

The range isn't a hard limit: if you're an expert in all of the above, we still want to talk to you. Not quite so experienced but passionate and keen to learn? Talk to us too.


LOCATION

Full-time on-site at one of our UK sites:

 - Cambridge: our central Cambridge site, alongside the team designing, building and expanding the Grid.

 - London: our London site.
